question: Can the cited procedural underground generator be legally and reproducibly acquired, and can the pinned official Isaac Sim 6.0.1 container pass the NVIDIA headless Compatibility Checker on this workstation?
method: Staged infrastructure execution: clone the paper-linked generator into an isolated external directory, freeze commit/remote/license/dependency evidence without modifying it, pull the pinned official Isaac Sim 6.0.1 container, record its immutable image identity, and run only the official headless Compatibility Checker. A one-world import smoke is permitted only if generator reuse and Isaac compatibility both pass; dataset generation and training remain prohibited.
baseline: Previous read-only audit found RTX 5090 D 32607 MiB, driver 580.173.02, Docker available, 641 GB free disk, no local Isaac runtime/image, an unverified 2022 paper-linked GitHub repository, and no located public repository for the 2024 graph-to-mesh implementation.

user_authorization.scope: Allow network acquisition and audit of the paper-linked generator, pull the pinned official Isaac Sim 6.0.1 image, run the NVIDIA Compatibility Checker, and proceed only to a one-world import/LiDAR smoke if all prerequisites pass; do not begin batch dataset generation or training.
user_authorization.confirmation_reference: User message after the proposed actions: 做吧

acceptance_criteria: The generator repository is acquired from the paper-linked remote and its exact commit, remote URL, working-tree state, LICENSE, dependency manifest, and entry points are recorded.
Generator reuse is marked blocked if no explicit compatible license is present; code is not copied into first-party source during this run.
The official Isaac Sim image is pinned to tag 6.0.1 and its immutable image ID/repository digest is recorded.
The official headless Compatibility Checker exits successfully and reports System checking result: PASSED; otherwise the run stops before any world import.
No privacy-consent opt-in is supplied, no existing containers are modified, and no unrelated Docker image or cache is deleted.
No batch map generation, dataset export, annotation, teacher generation, model training, ROS benchmark, or M-TARE comparison occurs.
A one-world import/LiDAR smoke is a separate documented substage and runs only if generator license, executable generation path, and Isaac compatibility are all valid.
stop_conditions: Less than 150 GB free disk before image pull
Repository remote mismatch or target path already occupied
Docker pull authentication, integrity, or storage failure
NVIDIA container runtime or GPU passthrough failure
Compatibility Checker result is not PASSED
expected_evidence: Generator provenance, commit, license, dependency, and entry-point audit
Pinned Isaac image ID and repository digest
Raw Compatibility Checker log and parsed pass/fail summary
Explicit decision on whether one-world import smoke is allowed
Machine-readable metrics, changed-file inventory, and completed/blocked run state

estimated_cost.compute: Network download, Docker image storage, and one short GPU Compatibility Checker execution; no dataset or training compute
